ev.q: Among children and adolescents aged 5–17 years, ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage was low overall, but highest among Asian and Hispanic or Latino children and adolescents.
Data collected during July 1–September 30, 2022, indicate that overall, 47.2% of children and adolescents received ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose
Monovalent booster dose coverage was low overall (14.7%)
Kaplan-Meier estimation methods were used to calculate cumulative ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage as of August 31, 2022.
Coverage in Black children aged 5–11 years was 4.0 to 33.6 percentage points lower than that among Asian, Hispanic, and other/multiple race children of the same age
Differences in ≥1-dose coverage were assessed by race and ethnicity and stratified by sociodemographic subgroups.
NIS-CCM is a nationally representative random-digit–dialed mobile telephone survey of households with children and adolescents aged 6 months–17 years.

methods_quotes.q: Kaplan-Meier estimation methods were used to calculate cumulative ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage as of August 31, 2022.
Differences in ≥1-dose coverage were assessed by race and ethnicity and stratified by sociodemographic subgroups.
Survey weights were used to adjust to the noninstitutionalized U.S. population of children and adolescents and to calibrate to CDC vaccine administration data.
For all analyses, p-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant.
Estimates were suppressed because they did not meet standards for data reliability (CI >20, relative SE >30, or sample size <30).
